chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from Nuʿaym ibn Ibrahim, from Mismāʿ Abū Sayyār, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
“The liability of the umm al-walad concerning the rights of people is upon her master.”
He عليه السلام said: “As for what is of the right of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, regarding the prescribed punishments, then that is upon her own body.”
And he عليه السلام said: “Retaliation applies from her in favor of slaves, and there is no qisas between the free person and the slave.”

key_terms.أُمُّ الْوَلَدِ: A slave woman who has borne a child to her master.
key_terms.الْحُدُودِ: Prescribed legal punishments set by the Sacred Law.
key_terms.جِنَايَتُهَا: Her offense or legal liability arising from injury or wrongdoing.
key_terms.حَقِّ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: The rights of Allah, especially in matters of divine legal claims.
key_terms.حُقُوقِ النَّاسِ: The rights owed to other human beings.
key_terms.قِصَاصَ: Legal retaliation in cases of bodily injury or killing.

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the legal liability of an umm al-walad and qisas between a free person and a slave?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the liability of an umm al-walad. It distinguishes between the rights of people, for which her master bears liability, and the rights of Allah in hudud, which are carried out on her own person; it also states that qisas applies with slaves, while there is no qisas between a free person and a slave.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5054 - Ibn Mahbub narrated from Nuaym ibn Ibrahim from Mismaʿ Abu Sayyar from Abu Abdullah (as) who said:
"The liability of umm Al-walad (a slave woman who has borne a child to her master) concerning the rights of people is upon her master."
Imam (as) also said: "As for the rights of Allah (swt), the Exalted, regarding prescribed punishments, that is upon her own body."
Furthermore, Imam (as) said: "Retribution (qiṣaṣ) applies between her and other slaves, but there is no retribution between a free person and a slave."
